what: Asked for 'the average rate at which the student does work against gravity' instead of 'the student's average power output'.
why: A person's power output includes far more than the work against gravity (muscles are roughly 25% efficient), so 'power output' has no single defensible value; the rate of work against gravity is exactly 250 watts.

why: A net force is the sum of the forces, not a push; the mixed wording blurs which force is meant.
